headline: Haiku passed the hidden strict check first time in all 12 cascade runs (0 escalations, 0 silent misses); all-Sonnet also 12/12. Paired tokens 439,437 to 648,395 (+47%); price -93.9% is an estimate (-59.6% at a 1:3 Haiku:Sonnet ratio). The weak-check hypothesis was not tested: the case set is too easy for Haiku.

On 6 cases (3 built to loop, 3 legitimate retries) both arms passed 12/12, no case got worse and nothing was falsely blocked, but tokens went up from A 5.71M to B 5.87M (+2.8%, inside the run-to-run noise). The guard refused once in 12 B runs and Jev was never called. Where B agents stopped early on the looping cases, they stopped before the guard had shown anything; the transcripts point to the B prompt's sentence that a guard is attached, not to the refusals. What blocks adoption: no token saving can be credited to the guard's refusals, the prompt sentence confounds the arms, and classify() would not guard the wrapped commands agents actually type (54 of 55 here). Top fix: re-measure with the guard sentence in both arms (arm A behind a silent placebo wrapper), on cases where plain Claude loops over several separate turns.

tool.name: context-curator
tool.commit: round-1 state e551872 + uncommitted curator.py; round-2 patch tool-change/curator-r2.patch

headline: Round 2 (ranked pointer list, Haiku 5.5, 4 cases x 2 repetitions, Jev live): both arms pass 8/8 and no case is worse; tokens 2.91M (A) -> 3.11M (B), +7% instead of +38% in round 1, but within the noise (B cheaper in 4 of 8 pairs). B agents barely used the list: all 8 B runs spent a turn reading the log head first. Top suggestion: make the pointer list self-sufficient (error-line previews, lines of the top 2-3 pointers) so that extra read turn goes away.

With the Jev confidence gate, Haiku agents passed A 11/12 vs B 12/12 on 6 blind-query tasks x 2 reps, but B cost 43% more tokens (8.84M -> 12.68M, 120 -> 173 model turns); no case worse. The extra turns were mostly agents waiting on a helper that took 100-300 s on a loaded machine (18 of 24 calls hit the 120 s Bash timeout), the gate fired on n5 r1/r2 and n6 r2 but saved nothing, and Jev never changed the useful #1. Top suggestion: make --provider none (codemap order) the default and keep Jev behind a flag.

tool.name: smart-context-trimming round 2 (agent run)
changes: extractCandidates: node failure block continues across the whitespace-only gap line; node-internal frames do not count toward FAILED_DETAIL_MAX (now 30)

headline: Round 2 (gap-line fix, node-only test digest): 10/10 pass in both arms again, session tokens -24% (4.29M -> 3.26M, 2 reps). Per case: js-root-exception -51% (was +8% in round 1), js-three-bugs -23%, js-one-bug -17%, dotnet-build -4% (was -35%), js-feature +12% (was +24%; B now 5 turns per rep, A 4 and 5). Not clearly better: the round-2 change does not touch dotnet-build output, yet its gain moved from -35% to -4% between rounds, so 2-rep noise is large. Top next suggestion: prove the live hook path (improvements.md suggestion 3).

On 6 two-story git batches (2 repetitions, Haiku 5.5 xhigh, Jev live) plain Haiku and Haiku with the round-2 verifier both pass 10 of 12 runs; c6 is wrong in both arms because its gold (S2 PASS) is inherited from the tool's own fixture, whose AC-coverage row cites a test that is on no branch. Tokens 7.54M -> 7.56M (+0.2%; round 1 was +28%), inside the repetition noise, with no case worse; the report still did not replace the agents' own merge and test runs. Top fix: rebuild the cases as harder multi-fault batches with a corrected c6 gold.

Round 2 (top round-1 fixes applied: ruleTier pinned by a test, checked rule ignores test globs; one Major from review fixed before measuring): both arms passed 12/12 on the first attempt, with no escalation. B cost $1.03 against $1.53 for all-Sonnet (-33%, price-weighted; round 1: -35%), and raw tokens went 3,407,036 -> 3,729,008 (+9.5% paired; within the run-to-run noise, mostly Sonnet-vs-Sonnet pairs). The saving is again the two lookup tasks on Haiku; the rule fix does not change any routed tier, because gate+sc takes the maximum with Jev, which still votes Sonnet for f1, d3, d5 and r1. Top fix: add an opt-in rules-plus-cascade policy that skips the Jev call when the prompt carries an automatic check, the only change that moves f1, d3, d5 and r1 to Haiku in the routed tier (estimated -70% to -95% against all-Sonnet, to be measured with harder cases).

headline: Still bad after the short-report change: plain Haiku 5.5 passes 7 of 8 runs and Haiku with the scanner 7 of 8 (A fails dcf-01 r2 on one decoy, B on one unlisted line in the same case), and B costs 84% more tokens (2.36M -> 4.34M, higher in 8 of 8 pairs, 7-10 model turns against 4-6). The short report cut report.md from about 12 KB to 2-4 KB, but not the extra turns: the agents still re-check candidates by hand. Top suggestion: skip the scan below about 2,000 lines and judge the tool only on a large case, where reading every file costs more than reading the report.

Round 2 (incomplete stories held in needs_decision, endpoint fix): both arms pass 6/6 on the same 3 batches, but the planner arm still uses 2.5x the tokens (654k -> 1,644k; was 2.7x). h2 got cheaper (112k/170k vs 248k/399k before), h1 B r2 cost 671k. Plain Haiku solves these batches in 2 turns, so the tool cannot beat A on cost here. Top suggestion: fix layer() so it stops splitting levels into chunks of 4 that push independent stories into extra waves.

Directional only (4 cases x 2 repetitions, Haiku 5.5): both arms get 8/8 right, but the curated view costs 38% more tokens than the plain log (2.58M -> 3.56M, higher in all 8 pairs); no case got worse. Jev answered every call but the view was only 17-44% smaller than the full log and B agents ran more turns (57 vs 42). Top fix: do not print the curated view as a replacement; keep the full log in a file and give only a ranked pointer list (or drop the curator until it can cut at least 70% of the log).

Plain Haiku 5.5 passes 7 of 8 runs and Haiku with the scanner 8 of 8 (the one A failure listed a "disabled with reason" decoy in the in-sample demo), but B costs 61% more tokens (2.01M -> 3.23M, higher in 8 of 8 pairs) for 1-5 extra turns reading a long report, and in dcf-04 both B runs missed 2 dead items that A found (6/8 vs 8/8). Jev's Tier A was precise (0 live items in Tier A of 25 unused-code candidates) but covers only 24 of 41 dead items. Top suggestion: make the report short (Tier A and B only, Tier C as a count).

On 4 small suites (8-15 tests, 6-7 criteria) plain Haiku 5.5 and Haiku with the tool pass every run (8/8 vs 8/8, identical verdicts in all 8 pairs); tokens 2.30M -> 2.27M (-1%, B lower in 4 of 8 pairs), which is noise. Jev marked 118 of 210 pairs skippable and no agent used a skipped test as evidence, but it also labelled the cart "name-only" trap partial_coverage (p 0.76-0.80), which both arms ignored. The suites are too small for any helper to show value; top suggestion: re-measure on a suite of 60+ tests where reading everything is costly.

Plain Haiku 5.5 and Haiku with the scanner both pass all 8 runs (visible and hidden tests green), tokens 4.70M -> 4.48M (-4.5%, B lower in 5 of 8 pairs; run-to-run noise on a single A case is 2.5x): the plain agent already read git history or fuzzed old against new and kept every planted guard. Jev changed the outcome where it was meant to (grs-02 formula 3.2 -> 4.6, flagged; grs-03 2.0 -> 0.7), and in 4 of 8 B runs the agent followed the defensive-mode step and added characterization tests (0 of 8 in A), but no case got a different result. Top suggestion: measure on tasks where the reason for a guard exists only in commit messages and the code gives no hint.

Directional only (4 cases x 2 repetitions, Haiku 5.5): plain Claude and Claude + jev_advisor both get 8/8 right, but the advisor arm spends about 7% more tokens (3.38M -> 3.63M, higher in 6 of 8 pairs, within the 2x spread between repetitions); no case got worse. Jev answered every call (about 1.1 s) but 4 of the 8 B agents wrote that a hint pointed at noise or only the symptom; the cases are too easy (1-2 KB sources name the cause) to show any value. Top fix: re-measure on a harder set where the cause is not visible in the source, with the hints reduced to the one anchor line.

On 6 two-story git batches (2 repetitions) plain Haiku 5.5 and Haiku with the verifier give the same answers (10 of 12 runs right in both arms; c6 wrong in all 4 runs), but the verifier arm spends 28% more tokens (7.03M -> 8.99M) because the agents re-checked the repo after reading the report; no case is worse. In c6 the tool said PASS for a story whose AC-coverage row cites a test that does not exist, and the agents overruled it. Top fix: print a short verdict-first report the agent can stop on, and check that a coverage row's test exists.

On 6 small cases (3 impossible, 3 legitimate retries) Haiku 5.5 never looped: it stopped after 1-2 runs on all impossible cases in both arms, so tokens barely moved (A 4.55M -> B 4.44M, -2.4%, inside the run-to-run noise) and pass is 11/12 vs 12/12 (the A miss is the agent declining to rerun). The Mod showed the agent nothing (0 notes, 0 Jev calls) and would have blocked the passing third run of flaky-twice in both repetitions (silent false block); no case is worse in B. The cases were too easy to show value. Top fix: re-measure on cases where the baseline really loops (and fix the fail-fail-pass false block in core.ts).

On 6 small checked tasks x 2 repetitions both arms passed 12/12 on the first attempt (no escalation needed), and the router's tier choice cost $0.97 against $1.51 for all-Sonnet (-35%, price-weighted; raw tokens the same, 3.25M). The whole saving is the two lookup tasks sent to Haiku (-95%); in the other 8 pairs B ran on Sonnet like A, and Jev never lowered a tier. The README's "14% of opus cost" is stale (current rules route 11 of 18 bench prompts to Sonnet), so it is not reproduced. Top fix: re-run the routing benchmark on the current prompts and pin ruleTier to it with a test, then make the "checked" rule ignore test globs.

After the rework (8 Major findings fixed, 15/15 tests), Jev clearly beats the tool's own rules offline (Recall@5 pass 4/5 vs 1/5 on eval/tasks.json, 5/6 vs 3/6 on new blind-query tasks), but Haiku agents found the right file in every case either way: 12/12 vs 12/12 over 6 new tasks x 2 reps, and B used 11% more tokens (10.76M -> 11.90M). No case worse. The ranking is better, but on these tasks it does not change the agent's answer.

On 3 harder batches (10-12 stories, x2 reps) the planner arm passed 6/6 and plain Haiku 5/6, but the planner arm used 2.7x the tokens (656k -> 1,747k). The one A failure is debatable (it held an independent story whose AC needs HR sign-off). The planner's own output was wrong on h2-portal (endpoint with a trailing period), and the agents corrected it. That bug is open.

On 4 small fixtures plain Haiku 5.5 already gets every case right (4/4), and so does Haiku with the planner, but the planner arm spends 2.5 times the tokens (429k -> 1,093k) on extra turns for reading and acting on the planner output. The fixtures are too easy to show any planner value, and one Critical bug is still open (layer() inverts the order when a prerequisite is incomplete). Fix it, then measure on larger, harder batches.

On 4 find-where-to-start tasks with Haiku 5.5, the same codemap pool in raw order (A) got all 4 right, and the pool ranked by the tool's rules plus Jev (B) got 3 of 4 (t3-refactor-decide missed the eval/shadow-hook group), using 11% more tokens (2.89M -> 3.22M). B is not better here and one case is worse, which is within agent noise at 4 cases; 8 Major review findings are open. Fix the failure paths, then measure on harder tasks.

After the fix (node --test ✖ recognised, repeated failures folded) trimming fires on all 5 tasks. Haiku 5.5 subagents still pass 20/20 in both arms, and total session tokens drop 18% (4.96M → 4.04M): js-one-bug −49%, dotnet-build −35%, js-three-bugs −25%, while js-root-exception (+8%) and js-feature (+24%) went up by about the run-to-run noise. Try it on real work before adopting.

On 5 real fix-the-build/test tasks × 2 runs with Haiku 5.5 subagents, all 20 sessions pass in both arms (no case worse). Total tokens −3% (5.10M → 4.97M), which is inside run-to-run noise; the real effect is only where trimming fired: dotnet-build −30% tokens and fewer turns (8 → 5–6). node --test failures (✖) are not recognised, so 3 of 5 tasks were never trimmed: fix that, then re-measure.

On 10 fixtures Claude reads 52% fewer tokens (98,400 → 47,223; −92% on the 6 long outputs the mod trims) and no critical line is lost. Jev was asked on 3 cases only. Fix the 3 Major review findings and measure on real logs before using it.

The re-frozen replay gate passes (control 33.5% upper bound against 30%), but the bound assumes the user acts at the 200k crossing: in the one session with a recorded compaction the user compacted 327 turns later, so the realized saving is unmeasured and the A/B (P3) has not run. Top suggestion: scope artifactDir to the experiment folder and raise staleTurns before any A/B, because a broad artifact folder gives 32 stale notes in one session.

On 6 pick-a-skill requests (4 with a skill as the answer, 2 needing none) with Haiku 5.5, plain Claude (A) with the full skill list picked right 12 of 12 times and Claude + the router hint (B, Jev live) also 12 of 12, so the hint changed no answer, while B used 72% more tokens (1.49M -> 2.56M) and about twice the turns (25 -> 44); no case got worse. The router itself was right on all 6 requests (0 Jev errors, ~0.8 s per call), but the cases were too easy to show value, and 3 Major tool findings stay open. Top fix: print the hint as one short line instead of a 2k-token JSON after a 30 KB list.

On the same 6 requests (Haiku 5.5, 2 repetitions), plain Claude (A) passed 12 of 12 and Claude + the one-line hint (B, Jev live) also 12 of 12, with no case worse; B used 9.2% more tokens (1.51M -> 1.65M) instead of the 72% of round 1, and the whole gap is two runs with a stray harness tool call (the other 10 pairs differ by -0.08% in total). The cases are still too easy to show value, so the verdict stays INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE. Top suggestion: measure on cases that plain Claude with the full listing gets wrong, with only Bash and the hand-back tool available to the pick agents.
